summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a router between its two segments: eth1 (172.20.1.0/24, peered with node2's enp8s0) and eth2 (172.20.2.0/24, peered with node3's enp8s0), with IPv4 forwarding enabled and docker0's class-E leak neutralized. Persisted this via a systemd oneshot service (antrieb-segments.service) plus /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf on node1, and via systemd-networkd static .network overrides on node2/node3 (enp8s0 static address + route, taking precedence over the existing en* DHCP catch-all). Verified node2<->node3 reachability through node1 both before and after restarting all three nodes one at a time; each node's boot_id changed and its addressing/forwarding/routing/connectivity recovered automatically without manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected topology/interfaces on all nodes; confirmed node1 eth1<->node2 enp8s0 and node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 as the two segments
Neutralized node1's docker0 (removed 240.127.1.1/24, brought interface down) per SONiC pre-config cleanup to avoid source-IP leakage
Assigned 172.20.1.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 172.20.2.1/24 to node1 eth2; assigned 172.20.1.2/24 to node2 enp8s0 and 172.20.2.2/24 to node3 enp8s0
Enabled global and per-interface IPv4 forwarding on node1 (ip_forward, conf.all.forwarding, conf.eth1/eth2.forwarding)
Added static routes on node2 (172.20.2.0/24 via 172.20.1.1) and node3 (172.20.1.0/24 via 172.20.2.1); verified node2<->node3 ping success through node1
Persisted node1 config via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf and a new systemd oneshot unit antrieb-segments.service (runs /usr/local/sbin/antrieb-segments.sh at boot, enabled for multi-user.target)

Persisted node2/node3 config via new /etc/systemd/network/10-enp8s0.network files (static Address + Route) that take precedence over the existing en* DHCP catch-all; applied live with networkctl reload
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all three nodes and confirmed healthy segment/forwarding/connectivity state

Restarted node1 via `reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, docker0 neutralization, and node2<->node3 connectivity all recovered automatically
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, confirmed changed boot_id, verified enp8s0 static address/route and connectivity to node3 recovered automatically
Restarted node3 via `reboot`, confirmed changed boot_id, verified enp8s0 static address/route and connectivity to node2 recovered automatically
Final bidirectional ping confirmation between node2 and node3 through node1 after all three restarts
